{{Quote|Our appeals have been ignored. It is now apparent that the Republic and the Jedi favor our enemies. General, you are our last hope against the Huk in this war.|A [[Unidentified Kaleesh holy man|Kaleesh]], to Grievous|<ref name="TEOR">{{StoryCite|story=The Eyes of Revolution|book=Star Wars: Visionaries}}</ref>}}
The '''Yam'rii''', also known as the '''Huk''', were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Insect/Legends|insects]] who hailed from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Huk/Legends|Huk]]. They had [[Mantis/Legends|mantis]]-like bodies, with large, multifaceted [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], thin torsos, knobby [[Exoskeleton|carapaces]], and pointed feet. Some members of the species had large, clipper-like [[Limb/Legends|forelimbs]] that could be used as weapons, while others featured two fingers instead. They stood two [[Meter/Legends|meters]] or more in height and walked about on two legs. Members of the species were known as stealthy predators who were easily angered. They loved meat and [[Egg/Legends|eggs]] and had no compunctions about eating the eggs of other sentient species.

After gaining access to [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] technology, the Yam'rii began an aggressive expansionist phase during which they sought out valuable materials for trade on nearby worlds and founded colonies to exploit them. They eventually reached the nearby planet [[Kalee/Legends|Kalee]], where they [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] the native [[Kaleesh/Legends|Kaleesh]]. The [[Reptile/Legends|reptilian]] captives fought back, and the two species were soon embroiled in a [[Huk War|war]]. After years of fighting, the Kaleesh gained the upper hand under the leadership of a [[Soldier/Legends|warrior]] named [[Grievous/Legends|Qymaen jai Sheelal]]&mdash;who later renamed himself Grievous. The Yam'rii were driven from their colonies and almost wiped out as the Kaleesh destroyed whole settlements and killed even civilian Yam'rii. The [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoids]] orchestrated several corrupt deals with members of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] to put a stop to the hostilities, and the Kaleesh were saddled with devastating punitive measures while the Yam'rii were portrayed as victims and thus faced no sanctions. Decades later, the Yam'rii were part of the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]]. During the [[Swarm War]], however, Yam'rii were among the insectoids who became [[Joiner]]s and fought alongside the [[Killik/Legends|Killiks]].

==Biology and appearance==
{{Dialogue|Han|We sure picked the wrong disguises for this job. I don't see anything that isn't a bug anywhere.|C-3PO|That's odd, Captain Solo. I don't see any bugs at all. The Verpine are a species of mantid, the Fefze are more closely related to beetles, and the Huk are much closer to vespids than&mdash;|Leia|I don't think Han actually meant bugs, Threepio. He was using the term pejoratively.|attr=C-3PO, Han Solo, and Leia Organa Solo encounter Yam'rii during the Swarm War|src=<ref name="DN3:TSW" />}}
[[File:RekForma-CouncilOfBlood1.jpg|thumb|left|upright|The Yam'rii Rek had two digits on each limb.]]
Yam'rii were [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]], bipedal<ref name="TSC" /> [[Insect/Legends|insects]].<ref name="SWE" /> They were distantly related to both the sentient [[Verpine/Legends|Verpine]]<ref name="CSWE III" /> and [[Vespid/Legends|vespid]] insects.<ref name="DN3:TSW">''[[Dark Nest III: The Swarm War]]''</ref> The Yam'rii had both male<ref name="CEII-1">[[Crimson Empire II: Council of Blood 1|''Crimson Empire II: Council of Blood'' 1]]</ref> and female [[Gender/Legends|sexes]].<ref name="CSWE II">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', Vol. II</ref>

Members of the [[Species/Legends|species]] were considered strange-looking by many non-Yam'rii.<ref name="FF CAN5">{{FactFile|22|CAN 1-6|Mos Eisley Cantina Characters}}</ref> Their giant,<ref name="CSWE II" /> [[Mantis/Legends|mantis]]-like bodies stood two [[Meter/Legends|meters]]<ref name="KK DB" /> or more in height<ref name="CEII-1" /> and were divided into three major sections: head, thorax, and abdomen.<ref name="TSC" /> They were strong, burly creatures,<ref name="CSWE III" /> although they remained stealthy despite their size.<ref name="SWC">''[[Star Wars Chronicles]]''</ref> Yam'rii were [[Diet/Legends|carnivorous]], subsisting on meat and [[Egg/Legends|eggs]]<ref name="CSWE III" />&mdash;and, according to rumor, their own kind. Yam'rii [[Blood/Legends|blood]] was green in [[Color/Legends|color]].<ref name="US" />

Large, multifaceted [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] dominated the beings' wedge-shaped heads.<ref name="KK DB" /><ref name="TSC" /> These orbs could be either gray<ref name="US" /> or red. At least some members of the species had pupil-like spots on their eyes.<ref name="CEII-1" /> Nostrils lay below the eyes,<ref name="CEII-3">[[Crimson Empire II: Council of Blood 3|''Crimson Empire II: Council of Blood'' 3]]</ref> although in most Yam'rii these were imperceptible. A mass of bumplike protrusions at the front of the head acted as a mouth and taste organ,<ref name="TSC" /> known to shudder at the prospect of a meal.<ref name="KK DB" /> In some specimens, the maw could be opened wide to reveal white [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]].<ref name="CEII-1" /> Dual knobby crests grew from the beings' heads with other bumps in between. A spiky ridge ran along the back of the head.<ref name="TSC" />

A long, narrow neck supported the head on broad, rounded shoulders. In many Yam'rii, both the neck and thorax were diamond-shaped in cross-section, with the more acute edges toward the front and back.<ref name="TSC" /> Other members of the species had two rows of raised bumps on the front and back of the torso instead.<ref name="CEII-2">[[Crimson Empire II: Council of Blood 2|''Crimson Empire II: Council of Blood'' 2]]</ref> The midsection was dominated by two [[Limb/Legends|arms]] held before the body mantis-like, the first of the double padded joints bent upward and the second downward.<ref name="TSC" /> In most Yam'rii, these arms were shaped like giant clippers: the upper limb had a barbed,<ref name="US" /> serrated cutting edge on its underside, and the lower part of the limb narrowed to a point;<ref name="TSC" /> together, both halves acted like shears.<ref name="US" /> Other Yam'rii, however, had two fingers and a thumb instead, trading deadly, natural weapons for the ability to perform fine manipation. Yam'rii forelimbs could grow so large as to drag the ground when the being walked.<ref name="CEII-1" /> The thorax tapered greatly at the waist, where the round, bulbous abdomen began. This posterior section came to a point in the back and featured striations along its length. The species' legs had a single knee joint and ended in jagged, pointed feet;<ref name="TSC" /> these were bifurcated into two digits in those Yam'rii with fine manipulator forelimbs.<ref name="CEII-1" />

Yam'rii were encased in hard [[Exoskeleton|carapaces]]<ref name="LoW">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/86/indexp2.html|text=The Story of General Grievous: Lord of War|int=The Story of General Grievous: Lord of War}}</ref> that were knobby, striated,<ref name="US" /> and colored gray,<ref name="CEII-1" /> brown,<ref name="US" /> or green.<ref name="SWE" /> A lighter shade sometimes re of the and abdomen.<ref name="TOTC">''[[Star Wars: The Original Trilogy Collection]]''</ref> Members of the species wore minimal clothing, such as cloth skirts,<ref name="TSC" /> belts, or [[Bandolier/Legends|bandoleers]] with pockets for carrying possessions.<ref name="US" />

==Society and culture==
The Yam'rii hailed from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Huk/Legends|Huk]], a world near the [[Kalee system/Legends|Kalee system]]<ref name="CSWE II" /> just outside [[Kadok Regions/Legends|Bitthævrian space]].<ref name="LoW" /> They were a technological culture with full access to [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]-capable [[Starship/Legends|spacecraft]]<ref name="US" /> and modern [[Droid/Legends|droids]]. In fact, the manufacturer [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]] gave its [[LOM-series protocol droid/Legends|LOM-series protocol droid]] series [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoid]] features in the hopes of appealing to Yam'rii and other insectoid consumers.<ref name="NEGD">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>

Members of the species were known for their quick tempers and lust for the property of others.<ref name="US" /> They showed little concern for non-Yam'rii; members of the species were known to eat the eggs of sentient species such as [[Quor'sav/Legends|Quor'sav]], for example, so mothers and caretakers of such creches had to keep careful watch when in a Yam'rii's company.<ref name="KK DB" /> After years of war, the species came to be regarded as downright savage by their wartime enemies.<ref name="LoE">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref> During these conflicts, the species was ruled by [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]].<ref name="GG DB">{{DB|character|generalgrievous|Grievous, General}}.</ref> Nevertheless, some Yam'rii did integrate into [[Galactic community|galactic society]] and form relationships with members of other species.<ref name="SC DB">{{DB|character|swillacorey|Corey, Swilla}}</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|Think about all the Alliance insects we've seen here. Verpine, Flakax, Fefze, Vratix, Huk.''"<br />"''I have been thinking about them. I've been thinking about them a lot.''"<br />"''If those governments fall, the Defense Force will be so busy in Alliance territory that it won't be able to keep the pressure on the Utegetu&mdash;much less carry the war to the rest of the Colony.|Leia Organa Solo and Han Solo, during the Dark Nest Crisis|<ref name="DN3:TSW" />}}
===Evolution and expansion===
The Yam'rii descended from non-sentient insects. At some point in their evolutionary path, they split from the line that would eventually become their distant relatives, the Verpine.<ref name="CSWE III" /> The Yam'rii regarded the planet Huk, located in [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]], as their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]].<ref name="CSWE II" /><ref name="EA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

Sometime between [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]]<ref name="EA" /> and generations before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Yam'rii established contact with the greater [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] and gained access to hyperspace technology.<ref name="US" /> They formed ties with the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and established themselves as important trading partners of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]].<ref name="LoE" /> The insectoid species decided it would be in their best interest to gain access to greater stores of natural resources, such as rarefied [[Mineral/Legends|minerals]]<ref name="US" /> and [[Ore/Legends|ore]],<ref name="LoE" /> to trade on the [[Galactic economy|galactic market]]. Settlers thus set off from Huk to colonize nearby planets, including the rainforest world [[Abbaji (Kalee system)|Abbaji]] and its neighbor [[Tovarskl]],<ref name="US" /> and to exploit the raw materials they afforded.<ref name="CWCG">''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]''</ref> Expansionist zeal blinded the species to any concern for pre-existing lifeforms or sentient species on the worlds the Yam'rii claimed.<ref name="US" />

The Yam'rii eventually reached the nearby Kalee [[Star system/Legends|system]].<ref name="US" /><ref name="GG DB" /> On the planet [[Kalee/Legends|Kalee]], they encountered a relatively primitive [[Reptile/Legends|reptilian]] species known as the [[Kaleesh/Legends|Kaleesh]].<ref name="US" /> Circa [[60 BBY/Legends|60 BBY]],<ref name="GAW">''[[Galaxy at War]]''</ref> the Yam'rii planted a colony on the world and began gathering the few resources they could find.<ref name="CWCG" /> These were deemed inadequate, however, and the insectoids turned to exporting a commodity they deemed much more lucrative: the Kaleesh themselves.<ref name="US" /> The insectoids corralled the reptilian species by the hundreds,<ref name="NEGAS">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> eventually [[Slavery/Legends|enslaving]] and selling millions on the galactic market.<ref name="CWCG" />

===The Huk War===
[[File:QymaenRonderuHuks.jpg|thumb|right|upright|During the Huk War, Yam'rii on Kalee battled the Kaleesh warriors Ronderu lij Kummar and Qymaen jai Sheelal at the Shrupak temple.]]
{{Main|Huk War}}
Several years before the Clone Wars,<ref name="CSWE II" /> the Yam'rii's new subjects rose up and began the conflict that came to be known as the [[Huk War]]. The Yam'rii found themselves crossing barbed cutter limbs with the slaves' [[Lig sword]]s, [[shoni spear]]s, and [[Slugthrower/Legends|slugthrowers]]. For two generations, the Yam'rii resisted the uprising and tried to contain it.<ref name="US" /> The rebellious Kaleesh proved to be formidable adversaries, however.<ref name="LoW" /> The Yam'rii came to be regarded by their enemies with more and more balefulness, and the word ''Huk'' took on a pejorative air, meaning not a race or a planet, but "[[Soul/Legends|soulless]] bug."<ref name="US" />

Years into the war, the tide began to turn. The Yam'rii found themselves losing several key battles, such as their [[Assault on Shrupak|assault]] on [[Shrupak]], considered the holiest temple in the Kaleesh religion. Several new Kaleesh resistance leaders sprang up, the companion [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]] [[Grievous/Legends|Qymaen jai Sheelal]] and [[Ronderu lij Kummar]] among them. The Yam'rii suffered defeat after defeat at the hands of Sheelal and his forces, and they soon found themselves on the defensive on Kalee.<ref name="US" />

The Yam'rii scored a key victory when they killed Kummar on the beaches of Kalee's [[Jenuwaa Sea]] and, it seemed, drove Sheelal into hiding.<ref name="US" /> The triumph was short-lived, however; Sheelal resurfaced, now calling himself Grievous and leading a corps of eight elite Kaleesh [[General/Legends|generals]], many of whom had led their own rebel forces across the planet.<ref name="LoW" /> United behind Grievous in a pan-Kaleesh [[Army/Legends|army]] known as the [[kolkpravis]],<ref name="GAW" /> the enemy found a new spirit, and the Yam'rii lost thousands to Kaleesh attacks. The Yam'rii made the decision to cut their losses and abandon their Kalee colony to their former slaves.<ref name="US" />

Grievous, however, was unsatisfied with this concession. Yam'rii colonists on nearby worlds soon found themselves besot by Kaleesh invaders who had adopted Yam'rii technology<ref name="NEGAS" /> and organized behind Grievous and his eight elites.<ref name="LoW" /> The Yam'rii were forced fully on the defensive<ref name="CWCG" /> as they lost battle after battle and colony after colony&mdash;the settlers wiped out to the last Yam'rii regardless of whether they were military or civilian.<ref name="LoE" /><ref name="TEOR">{{StoryCite|story=The Eyes of Revolution|book=Star Wars: Visionaries}}</ref> The Yam'rii were pursued even into their home system: the planet Huk itself was overrun by Kaleesh warriors. The enemy seemed unstoppable, rampaging as far afield as Tovarskl.<ref name="US" /> With their numbers so severely depleted, the Yam'rii realized that they faced nothing less than the extinction of their species.<ref name="CWCG" />

The Yam'rii pulled strings with their allies in the Trade Federation<ref name="US" /> to compel the Republic to stop the Kaleesh's retribution.<ref name="NEGAS" /> After several backroom deals the Republic decided to intervene in the conflict,<ref name="CWCG" /> and the [[Judicial Department/Legends|Republic Judicial Department]]<ref name="US" /> dispatched fifty [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]<ref name="LoW" /> under the command of [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] [[T'chooka D'oon]] and [[Jmmaar/Legends|Jmmaar]] to mediate a settlement. The Yam'rii claimed that the Kaleesh were the aggressors in the conflict,<ref name="CSWE II" /> and corruption ensured that the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] pressured the Jedi to believe them.<ref name="US" /> The Jedi did as they were told: they chastised the Kaleesh for their belligerence,<ref name="LoE" /> ordered them to pay war indemnities, demanded the return of worlds they had conquered, and imposed economic sanctions.<ref name="US" /> Several Kaleesh leaders faced war trials.<ref name="CWCG" /> Despite the Kaleesh's protestations that they were the victims,<ref name="LoE" /> the war finally came to an end with a Yam'rii victory.<ref name="US" />

Now with the full support of the Republic, the Yam'rii reclaimed their erstwhile colonies. They destroyed those structures the Kaleesh had built during their occupation, including burial grounds considered sacred to the reptilians. The Kaleesh petitioned the Republic and the Trade Federation to put a stop to the desecration, but the galactic government stood behind the Yam'rii.<ref name="US" /><ref name="NEGAS" />

The Galactic Republic's response to the [[Huk War|Yam'rii crisis]] established precedent for the use of paramilitaries by the galactic government. [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]] cited the precedent in arguing for a similar response to problems on the planet [[Yinchorr/Legends|Yinchorr]].<ref name="DP">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>

===Later conflicts===
Unbeknownst to the insectoids, Grievous and his kolkpravis made one final push to punish them for desecrating burial grounds on the colony world [[Oben]], but his [[Martyr|ship]] was crashed by the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]]&mdash;IGBC&mdash;a commercial organization looking to bring the Kaleesh into their control as an enforcer. [[Bentilais san Sk'ar]], one of Grievous' [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenants]], survived the crash-landing and eventually led another attack on Oben. The Yam'rii fled, ceding control to the Kaleesh.<ref name="GAW" />

For a time, the Yam'rii were left to their own devices. However, after the formation of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] and the outbreak of the Clone Wars in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the Yam'rii colonists on Tovarskl received some unexpected guests: their one-time foe Grievous and an army of [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]]. The Kaleesh, having been turned into a [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] by the IGBC and, via his affiliation to that organization, now a general for the Confederacy, ordered the droids to [[Battle of Tovarskl|attack]]. The Yam'rii on the world were slaughtered.<ref name="US" />

Huk remained outside the influence of various galactic governments until at least [[17 ABY/Legends|17 ABY]].<ref name="EA" /> Eventually, the Yam'rii joined the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]].<ref name="DN3:TSW" /> By this time, they were still commonly referred to as the Huk. When the [[Swarm War]] broke out in [[36 ABY]], disgruntled Yam'rii on Huk received overtures from the [[Killik/Legends|Killiks]] encouraging them to overthrow their government and side with [[the Colony]] against the Galactic Alliance.<ref name="CSWE II" /> Some Yam'rii responded and became [[Joiner]]s, addicted to the [[Gorog|Dark Nest's]] black [[Membrosia/Legends|membrosia]]. Alliance operatives [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]], and [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] saw them among other targeted insectoid species in the [[Lizil|nest]] known as [[Lizil (Hive)|Lizil]].<ref name="DN3:TSW" /> Knowing that such a coup, if it came along with others around the galaxy, would spread the Alliance forces thin, Jedi arrived to stymie any rebellion.<ref name="CSWE II" /> In [[137 ABY]], after the fall of the Galactic Alliance to the forces of [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Krayt]], the Yam'rii were once again isolated and outside the reach of extraplanetary governments.<ref name="EA" />

==Yam'rii in the galaxy==
[[File:KitikKeedkak-TheSagaCollection.jpg|thumb|left|Kitik Keed'kak integrated into galactic society, although she craved the eggs of other sentients, such as Quor'sav.]]
Yam'rii were aggressive expansionists who founded numerous colonies on disparate worlds, conquering any who stood in their way. Although many members of the species distinguished themselves in war,<ref name="US" /> a few earned a name for themselves in other pursuits.<ref name="KK DB" /><ref name="CSWE III" />

[[Kitik Keed'kak]] was one such being. She was a powerfully built,<ref name="FF CAN5" /> sly, and stealthy member of her species.<ref name="KK DB" /> Although she was handy with all sorts of technology, her love for eggs consumed her to the point that in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], she was virtually stalking the Quor'sav mother [[Kal'Falnl C'ndros]] to eat the [[Bird/Legends|avian's]] brood.<ref name="KK DB" /><ref name="KK CCG">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Kitik Keed'kak}}</ref> Keed'kak had a penchant to upbraid and excoriate anyone who distracted her from her goal<ref name="TSC" />&mdash;with the exception of her friend, the young [[Human/Legends|Human]] thief [[Swilla Corey]].<ref name="SC DB" /> Keed'kak was drinking at the [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Mos Eisley Cantina]] on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] in 0 BBY on the same day that [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] were looking for passage to [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]].<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> At the moment Kenobi sliced up the [[Aqualish/Legends|Aqualish]] thug [[Ponda Baba/Legends|Ponda Baba]], Keed'kak was directing Corey to a [[Pacithhip/Legends|Pacithhip]] [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] in the [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] named [[Ketwol/Legends|Ketwol]].<ref name="SC DB" /> She later left the cantina as the [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] [[Davin Felth/Legends|Davin Felth]] entered the building.<ref name="When the Desert Wind Turns: The Stormtrooper's Tale">{{StoryCite|story=When the Desert Wind Turns: The Stormtrooper's Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref>

A Yam'rii of the fingered variety, [[Rek (majordomo)|Rek]], was a [[Majordomo/Legends|majordomo]] and [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguard]] who worked for the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] gangster [[Grappa (Hutt)|Grappa]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] in the days of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].<ref name="CSWE III" /> Rek was stationed at Grappa's base on the planet [[Genon]]. In [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]], Rek was present when Grappa received the [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoner]] [[Forma]] from the [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] [[Sol Mon]].<ref name="CEII-1" /> The Yam'rii later accompanied Grappa to the planet [[Smarck]] to meet the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Macus Kayniph]].<ref name="CEII-2" /> When Grappa later murdered Kayniph at his palace on Genon, Rek was among those gassed by his master to cover up the killing and make it appear to be part of a larger accident.<ref name="CEII-4">[[Crimson Empire II: Council of Blood 4|''Crimson Empire II: Council of Blood'' 4]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|This turned out to be one of my favorite Star Wars illustrations in a while. It's just appealing to me in a B-monster movie kind of way with the attacking Huk insectoids, creepy masks and green blood spattered swords.|Joe Corroney|<ref name="joecorroney32">{{Blog|joecorroney|32|Die Jedi Die&hellip; One More Time!}}</ref>}}
[[File:KitikKeedkakSketch-CantinaRollCall.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Actor Jack Purvis operated the Yam'rii puppet from under its skirt on the London set of ''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope''.]]
[[Stuart Freeborn]] designed the model that would become the Yam'rii in [[Wikipedia:England|England]] during production of the cantina sequence of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], released in [[1977]]. The actual prop used in the film was a puppet constructed by the special effects team in [[Wikipedia:London|London]] and filmed on set as part of principal photography.<ref name="CRC">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iv/bts/article/f20030502/index.html|text=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases|int=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases}}</ref> The character was referred to as the "Praying Mantis" during production.<ref name="KK DB" /> An uncredited [[Jack Purvis]], the same actor who portrayed the chief [[Jawa/Legends|Jawa]] in the film,<ref name="CRC" /> hid under the [[Alien/Legends|alien's]] skirt<ref name="CRC image">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iv/bts/article/f20030502/index.html|text=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases|int=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases}}, Kitik Keed'kak illustration</ref> and operated it via strings attached to its limbs.<ref name="SWC" /> Despite being one of the most intricate and complex props created for the scene, the Praying Mantis is difficult to spot in the final film.<ref name="CRC" /> Jack's son [[Andy Purvis]] played the puppet during one day of filming.<ref name="Andy Purvis">{{InsiderCite|218|Andy Purvis: A Bug's Life}}</ref>

The species was first identified as the Yam'rii&mdash;and the individual seen in ''A New Hope'' as Kitik Keed'kak&mdash;in [[Decipher]]'s [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]] in [[1995]]. The card featuring the character established several key features of the species, such as their great strength and love for eggs. The card's statistics make Keed'kak one of the more physically powerful characters in the game, although she is immediately lost if the card representing the Quor'sav mother Kal'falnl C'ndros is present at the same location.<ref name="KK CCG" /> The same character appears in the background of [[Pablo Hidalgo]]'s [[A Hunter's Fate: Greedo's Tale (webstrip)|''A Hunter's Fate: Greedo's Tale'' webstrip]].

Nearly thirty years after the "Praying Mantis" appeared in ''A New Hope'', ''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]'' and ''[[The Eyes of Revolution]]'' detailed an insectoid species known as the Huk. The sources revealed that the Huk had fought a long war with another species, the Kaleesh, and their leader, General Grievous. [[Abel G. Peña]] decided to merge the Huk and the Yam'rii in his article ''[[Unknown Soldier: The Story of General Grievous]]''. At the time he wrote the article, little was known about either. He had always considered the Yam'rii to be one of the more interesting-looking and compelling of ''[[Star Wars]]''{{'}} various insectoid races.<ref name="abelgpena53">{{Blog|abelgpena|53|Endnotes for The Story of General Grievous, Part 1: The Unknown Soldier}}</ref> [[Joe Corroney]] provided the illustrations for the article, including a piece in which Grievous&mdash;in his guise as Qymaen jai Sheelal&mdash;and his partner, Ronderu lij Kummar, defend the Shrupak temple from the insectoids. Corroney reports in his blog that he enjoyed creating the piece because the Yam'rii are in his opinion "otherworldly and unique looking." He cites the illustration as one of his favorite ''Star Wars'' works because it reminds him of a B-monster movie.<ref name="joecorroney32" /> The novel [[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']], published in [[2012]] by [[Del Rey]] and written by [[James Luceno]], mentions a "Yam'rii crisis" sometime before the Clone Wars. Little context is provided about the conflict, so its relationship to the Huk War is unclear.<ref name="DP" />

While Peña's article was in editing in [[2005]], the novel ''[[Dark Nest III: The Swarm War]]'', by [[Troy Denning]], was published. It includes a scene in which the droid C-3PO describes the Huk as "vespid"&mdash;wasp-like&mdash;rather than mantid, like the Yam'rii have been depicted. Peña speculates that this must refer to some aspect of the species other than their appearance, but he admits that this is currently a discrepancy.<ref name="abelgpena53" /> The entry for the Yam'rii in ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' says that "it was believed that the Huk species was an offshoot of the Yam'rii," implying that the two were not in fact the same.<ref name="CSWE III" /> This contradicts other entries in that same work, however, so it is assumed to be an error.

Mantis-like aliens appear in a few sources but have not been specifically identified as Yam'rii. For example, one such character walks by in the [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] crowd in [[Chapter 21 (Star Wars: Clone Wars)|''Clone Wars Chapter 21'']], and a mantid [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] with serrated arms is a member of the [[Guild Council]], the leading body of the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild/Legends|Bounty Hunters' Guild]], in ''[[The Mandalorian Armor]]''.<ref name="The Mandalorian Armor">''[[The Mandalorian Armor]]''</ref>
